primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial renal glucosuria due to SLC5A2 dysfunction
mechanism: SLC5A2 encodes SGLT2, the high-capacity sodium-glucose cotransporter on the apical brush-border membrane of early proximal tubular cells. Loss reduces reabsorption of filtered glucose despite normal plasma glucose.
vignette: A healthy 19-year-old repeatedly has marked glucosuria on routine urinalysis despite normal fasting plasma glucose and hemoglobin A1c. There is no aminoaciduria, phosphaturia, or bicarbonate wasting. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic loss-of-function variant in SLC5A2.
lead: Which renal transport process is most directly impaired?
correct: Apical sodium-glucose cotransport in the early proximal tubule
distractors: Basolateral facilitated glucose transport through GLUT2 in proximal tubular cells
Apical sodium-glucose cotransport through SGLT1 in the late proximal tubule
Apical sodium-hydrogen exchange in the proximal tubule
Apical sodium-phosphate cotransport in the proximal tubule
distractor_notes: GLUT2 mediates basolateral glucose exit after cellular uptake; SLC5A2 encodes the apical SGLT2 transporter.
SGLT1 reabsorbs a smaller residual glucose load in later proximal segments and is encoded by SLC5A1, not SLC5A2.
NHE3 participates in sodium/bicarbonate handling but does not cause isolated normoglycemic glucosuria when SLC5A2 is mutated.
Sodium-phosphate cotransport affects phosphate handling rather than isolated renal glucose reabsorption.
key_expl: SGLT2, encoded by SLC5A2, is expressed on the apical membrane of early proximal tubular cells and reabsorbs most filtered glucose. Loss causes isolated glucosuria despite normal blood glucose.
objective: Link familial renal glucosuria to impaired apical SGLT2-mediated sodium-glucose cotransport in the early proximal tubule.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Scott syndrome due to ANO6/TMEM16F dysfunction
mechanism: ANO6 encodes TMEM16F, a calcium-activated phospholipid scramblase. Upon strong platelet activation it externalizes phosphatidylserine, providing an anionic membrane surface for tenase and prothrombinase assembly and efficient thrombin generation. Loss causes Scott syndrome.
vignette: A young adult has recurrent bleeding after surgery and dental procedures. Platelet count, prothrombin time, and activated partial thromboplastin time are normal. Platelet aggregation to standard agonists is largely preserved. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in ANO6.
lead: Which platelet membrane event is most directly impaired?
correct: Calcium-dependent externalization of phosphatidylserine on activated platelets
distractors: Fibrinogen binding to activated glycoprotein IIb/IIIa
von Willebrand factor binding to glycoprotein Ib
Release of ADP from platelet dense granules
Surface expression of P-selectin after alpha-granule release
distractor_notes: GPIIb/IIIa-dependent fibrinogen binding mediates platelet aggregation and is the Glanzmann pathway, not the ANO6 scramblase defect.
GPIb-vWF binding mediates platelet adhesion and is distinct from the procoagulant phosphatidylserine surface.
Dense-granule ADP release amplifies platelet activation but is not the defining membrane-scrambling defect of Scott syndrome.
P-selectin reflects alpha-granule secretion and does not substitute for phosphatidylserine exposure.
key_expl: TMEM16F/ANO6 is the calcium-activated scramblase that moves phosphatidylserine to the outer platelet membrane, creating the catalytic surface for coagulation-complex assembly. Its loss causes Scott syndrome.
objective: Link Scott syndrome to defective ANO6/TMEM16F-mediated phosphatidylserine externalization on activated platelets.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: KIF1A is an ATP-dependent kinesin motor that transports neuronal cargo along axonal microtubules. Disease-causing variants commonly disrupt the motor domain and reduce microtubule-based cargo transport.
vignette: A child has global developmental delay, progressive lower-extremity spasticity, peripheral neuropathy, optic atrophy, and cerebellar atrophy. Trio sequencing identifies a de novo pathogenic missense variant in the motor domain of KIF1A.
lead: Which normal function of the affected protein is most directly disrupted?
correct: ATP-dependent transport of neuronal cargo along axonal microtubules
distractors: Actin-dependent transport of vesicles by myosin motors
Retrograde transport of endosomes by cytoplasmic dynein
Assembly of neurofilament intermediate filaments
Fusion of synaptic vesicles with the presynaptic membrane by SNARE proteins
distractor_notes: Myosin motors move cargo on actin rather than representing the KIF1A kinesin-microtubule pathway.
Dynein is the major retrograde microtubule motor; KIF1A is a kinesin-family cargo transporter.
Neurofilament assembly is distinct from KIF1A-mediated axonal cargo transport.
SNARE-mediated vesicle fusion is a membrane-fusion step downstream of transport and is not KIF1A's motor function.
key_expl: KIF1A is an ATP-dependent kinesin motor protein that transports cargo along axonal microtubules. Motor-domain pathogenic variants can reduce motility, microtubule binding, run length, or velocity.
objective: Associate KIF1A-related neurologic disease with impaired ATP-dependent axonal microtubule cargo transport.

outline: AMER1-related osteopathia striata with cranial sclerosis
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
discipline: Bone Biology / Signal Transduction / Medical Genetics
diagnosis: AMER1-related osteopathia striata with cranial sclerosis
mechanism: AMER1 acts as an inhibitor of canonical WNT signaling by promoting beta-catenin ubiquitination and degradation. Loss of AMER1 causes nuclear beta-catenin accumulation, increased WNT signaling and osteoblastic activity, producing cranial sclerosis and metaphyseal striations.
vignette: A girl has macrocephaly, hypertelorism, hearing loss, dense cranial bones, and linear metaphyseal striations on long-bone radiographs. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous loss-of-function variant in AMER1.
lead: Which molecular consequence most directly follows from loss of the affected protein?
correct: Accumulation of beta-catenin with increased canonical WNT signaling
distractors: Accelerated degradation of beta-catenin with reduced canonical WNT signaling
Constitutive activation of fibroblast growth factor receptor 3
Failure of RANK-mediated osteoclast differentiation
Constitutive activation of transforming growth factor beta-1 signaling
distractor_notes: AMER1 normally helps restrain canonical WNT signaling; loss decreases rather than accelerates beta-catenin degradation.
FGFR3 activation causes achondroplasia-spectrum disorders and is not the AMER1 mechanism.
RANK-pathway defects cause osteoclast-poor osteopetrosis rather than the AMER1/WNT phenotype.
TGFB1 gain of function causes Camurati-Engelmann disease, a distinct hyperostotic disorder.
key_expl: AMER1 promotes beta-catenin ubiquitination/degradation and restrains canonical WNT signaling. Loss permits beta-catenin accumulation and increased osteoblastic WNT activity, producing osteopathia striata with cranial sclerosis.
objective: Link AMER1 loss to increased beta-catenin/canonical WNT signaling in osteopathia striata with cranial sclerosis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: RBM20 is a cardiac RNA-binding splicing regulator whose major targets include TTN and other sarcomeric/ion-handling transcripts. Pathogenic RBM20 dysfunction alters titin isoform splicing and can cause aggressive familial dilated cardiomyopathy with arrhythmias.
vignette: A 28-year-old develops severe nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy and ventricular arrhythmias. Several relatives developed cardiomyopathy before age 40. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in RBM20.
lead: Which normal molecular function is most directly associated with the affected gene product?
correct: Regulation of alternative splicing of titin and other cardiac pre-mRNAs
distractors: DNA mismatch repair during cardiomyocyte replication
Transcriptional activation of mitochondrial DNA
Ubiquitination of damaged sarcomeric proteins for proteasomal degradation
Calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum through ryanodine receptors
distractor_notes: RBM20 is an RNA-binding splicing regulator, not a DNA mismatch-repair protein.
RBM20 regulates nuclear pre-mRNA splicing rather than mitochondrial-DNA transcription.
Proteasomal quality control is distinct from RBM20-mediated alternative splicing.
Ryanodine receptors mediate calcium release; some ion-handling transcripts are RBM20 splicing targets, but RBM20 itself is not a calcium channel.
key_expl: RBM20 is a key cardiac alternative-splicing factor. A major target is TTN pre-mRNA, whose splice isoforms determine titin mechanical properties; RBM20 variants are an established cause of familial DCM.
objective: Link RBM20 cardiomyopathy to abnormal alternative splicing of TTN and other cardiac transcripts.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Biallelic SPINT2 loss causes syndromic congenital sodium diarrhea, a severe neonatal sodium-rich secretory diarrhea associated with extraintestinal anomalies such as choanal or anal atresia and corneal disease; SPINT2 encodes a Kunitz-type serine-protease inhibitor.
vignette: A neonate has persistent profuse watery diarrhea, hyponatremia, metabolic acidosis, and extremely high fecal sodium concentration. Examination also shows choanal atresia and corneal erosions. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SPINT2.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains this combination of findings?
distractors: Congenital chloride diarrhea
Microvillus inclusion disease
Congenital tufting enteropathy
Glucose-galactose malabsorption
distractor_notes: Congenital chloride diarrhea causes chloride-rich diarrhea with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis rather than high-sodium diarrhea with acidosis and syndromic anomalies.
Microvillus inclusion disease causes severe neonatal diarrhea but has a MYO5B/STX3 trafficking phenotype rather than the SPINT2-associated choanal/corneal syndrome.
Tufting enteropathy can cause congenital diarrhea but is associated with epithelial tufting and EPCAM-related disease, not this SPINT2 syndromic pattern.
Glucose-galactose malabsorption is an SGLT1 disorder whose diarrhea improves when glucose/galactose are removed and does not cause the characteristic extraintestinal anomalies.
key_expl: SPINT2 loss causes a syndromic form of congenital sodium diarrhea characterized by neonatal sodium-rich watery diarrhea and associated anomalies including choanal/anal atresia and corneal disease.
objective: Recognize SPINT2-related syndromic congenital sodium diarrhea from neonatal sodium-rich diarrhea plus characteristic extraintestinal anomalies.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: KISS1R is the kisspeptin receptor expressed on GnRH neurons. Kisspeptin activation of KISS1R depolarizes GnRH neurons and stimulates GnRH secretion; inactivating KISS1R variants can cause normosmic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and failure of normal pubertal activation.
vignette: An 18-year-old has absent pubertal development, low testosterone, and inappropriately low luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone concentrations. Sense of smell is normal and pituitary MRI is normal. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in KISS1R.
lead: Which signaling step is most directly impaired?
correct: Kisspeptin-mediated activation of hypothalamic GnRH neurons
distractors: GnRH binding to its receptor on pituitary gonadotrophs
LH binding to its receptor on Leydig cells
Inhibin B suppression of pituitary FSH secretion
Testosterone binding to the androgen receptor in target tissues
distractor_notes: The pituitary GnRH receptor is downstream of hypothalamic GnRH secretion and is not encoded by KISS1R.
LH receptor signaling occurs in the gonad and is downstream of the low gonadotropin state.
Inhibin B feedback modulates FSH but does not initiate the kisspeptin-GnRH pubertal signal.
Androgen receptor signaling is downstream of gonadal testosterone production.
key_expl: KISS1R is the receptor for kisspeptin on GnRH neurons. Kisspeptin-KISS1R signaling activates and depolarizes GnRH neurons, stimulating GnRH release and normal pubertal progression.
objective: Link KISS1R-related hypogonadotropic hypogonadism to loss of kisspeptin stimulation of hypothalamic GnRH neurons.
clues: low sex steroid with low/inappropriately normal gonadotropins

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Molybdenum cofactor deficiency due to MOCS1 dysfunction
mechanism: MOCS1 participates in the first step of molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis, converting GTP to cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate. Loss of molybdenum cofactor disables sulfite oxidase and other molybdoenzymes; sulfite accumulation is the major driver of severe neonatal neurotoxicity.
vignette: A neonate develops refractory seizures and rapidly progressive encephalopathy. Laboratory studies show elevated urinary sulfite and S-sulfocysteine with low uric acid. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in MOCS1.
lead: Which impaired reaction most directly explains the neurotoxic metabolite accumulation?
distractors: Remethylation of homocysteine to methionine
Conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA
Oxidation of homogentisate to maleylacetoacetate
Conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine
distractor_notes: Homocysteine remethylation depends on folate/cobalamin pathways rather than molybdenum cofactor.
Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase requires adenosylcobalamin and is unrelated to sulfite accumulation.
Homogentisate oxidase deficiency causes alkaptonuria, not neonatal sulfite neurotoxicity.
Phenylalanine hydroxylation uses tetrahydrobiopterin and does not account for sulfite accumulation.
key_expl: Sulfite oxidase requires molybdenum cofactor and catalyzes sulfite-to-sulfate oxidation. In molybdenum cofactor deficiency, loss of sulfite oxidase activity causes toxic sulfite accumulation and severe neonatal neurologic injury.
objective: Link MOCS1-related molybdenum cofactor deficiency to impaired sulfite oxidation and neurotoxic sulfite accumulation.

mechanism: The ecological fallacy occurs when an association observed using aggregate group-level data is incorrectly assumed to hold at the individual level; group-level joint distributions do not establish individual-level exposure-outcome relationships.
vignette: Investigators compare 50 counties and find that counties with higher average household income have lower cardiovascular mortality. They then conclude that within every county, an individual person with a higher household income necessarily has a lower cardiovascular mortality risk than a lower-income neighbor, even though no individual-level income and outcome data were collected.
lead: Which error in interpretation is being made?
distractors: Simpson paradox
Recall bias
Regression dilution bias
Immortal time bias
distractor_notes: Simpson paradox refers to reversal or major change of an association after combining or stratifying groups; the defining error here is group-to-individual inference without individual data.
Recall bias concerns differential memory/reporting of prior exposure and is not relevant to aggregate county data.
Regression dilution reflects measurement error in a continuous predictor, not inference across levels of analysis.
Immortal time bias arises from time-dependent exposure classification and is unrelated to ecological inference.
key_expl: The study observes an aggregate county-level association but infers an individual-level relationship without individual-level data. That cross-level inference is the ecological fallacy.
objective: Recognize ecological fallacy when group-level associations are incorrectly generalized to individuals.
clues: individual conclusion drawn from group association

system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
outline: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
mechanism: The Four Habits Model organizes an outpatient clinical encounter into four communication tasks: Invest in the beginning, Elicit the patient's perspective, Demonstrate empathy, and Invest in the end.
vignette: During an outpatient visit, a physician first builds rapport and negotiates the agenda, then asks about the patient's ideas and how the illness affects daily life, explicitly acknowledges the patient's emotions, and closes by explaining the plan, involving the patient in decisions, and confirming next steps.
lead: Which communication framework is best illustrated?
distractors: NURSE
VALUE
Ask-Tell-Ask
Best Case/Worst Case
distractor_notes: NURSE is focused specifically on responding to emotion and does not structure the entire clinical encounter into four sequential habits.
VALUE is designed for clinician-family communication in ICU conferences.
Ask-Tell-Ask is an iterative information-sharing micro-skill rather than a full encounter framework.
Best Case/Worst Case is a scenario-planning shared-decision tool for high-stakes treatment alternatives.
key_expl: The vignette follows the Four Habits sequence: Invest in the beginning, Elicit the patient's perspective, Demonstrate empathy, and Invest in the end.
objective: Recognize the Four Habits Model from its four sequential physician communication tasks across a clinical encounter.
